note: Orbit Weekly — the bundled sample publication (FR-H3). Rows carry the Content API field names the shim reads by dotted path; tags and authors are referenced by slug and hydrated by packages/library/src/orbit-weekly.ts, which also derives every count. The post and page fixture subjects live under `subjects` as whole rows, never in `posts`, so no feed, Source or count can reach them. The tag and author subjects (Story 5.13, FR-D22) CANNOT be hidden that way — an archive's posts come from the feed, so a hidden taxonomy would render an empty archive — and are therefore SLUGS of rows that already exist, which is also what makes each a stated choice rather than an accident of sort order.

comments.html: I renew mine in October too, and I had never once thought about why. It was when my first host billed me.

replies.html: That is the most common answer I got, and the host closed in 2013 for two of them.

comments.html: Is the list public? I think one of mine might be on it.

replies.html: It is at the end of the issue — the spreadsheet link.

comments.html: The line about one dollar a month and one afternoon a decade is going on my wall.

I kept a site on the same address from 2001 until last year, when I finally let it lapse. Reading this, I wish I had not. It was not that anybody read it — by the end I think three people a year arrived there, most of them looking for a recipe I posted in 2006 — but it was the one place on the internet that was entirely mine, arranged the way I wanted, and nobody could reorder it or put anything next to it. I moved the words to a newsletter platform. The words are all still there. The place is not, and I had not understood until this week that the place was the point.

replies.html: Thank you for writing this. The domain may still be available — it is worth checking.

comments.html: Two of the universities on the list are mine. I will say nothing more.
The shell script is lovely. I would add a user agent so people can tell who is knocking.

replies.html: Seconded — and a contact address in it, so they can tell you to stop.

comments.html: Does the Internet Archive answer count as still live if the owner is gone?
I would read an entire issue on the estates that keep paying.
Seven homepages, same window width — I love that you controlled for that.

replies.html: The window was 1280 wide. Every one of them looked different at 1440.
